data.title: DDCore: use std::call_once for threadsafe MultipoleField initialization
data.author: wdconinc
data.body:
MultipoleField previously used a thread-unsafe boolean flag, which led to data races during multithreaded running:
- one thread would get into the if block and immediately set the flag,
- the next thread would stay out of the if block and assume initialization had already happened,
- only then would the first thread complete initialization.

This results in incorrect fields in the second thread (for the first event only).

This PR converts to using call_once on a private initialize function (see `SurfaceManager` for this approach). Most of the diff is just indentation correction.

BEGINRELEASENOTES
- DDCore: use std::call_once for threadsafe MultipoleField initialization

ENDRELEASENOTES

data.title: Fail ACTS master CI on deprecation warnings after building
data.author: jmcarcell
data.body:
The workflow uses `-Werror` for k4ActsTracking but exempts `-Wdeprecated-declarations` and `-Wcpp`. [A recent successful run](https://github.com/key4hep/k4ActsTracking/actions/runs/42815168621) has three deprecated material API warnings and a deprecated-header `#warning`.

Explicitly disable warnings-as-errors when building ACTS itself. Check only k4ActsTracking compiler diagnostics after its build and tests, so upstream warnings do not fail the job. data.title: perf(build): only look for the Python interpreter in DD4hepConfig
data.author: chrisburr
data.body:
I've been looking at speeding up the cmake configuration time in LHCb and I found that `FIND_PACKAGE(Python)` was being called many times. This ends up being slow due to `python-config` being called several time and the build we use of Python has a high startup overhead.

Unless DD4hep was built with Geant4 there is no need to look for the `Development` components.

This ends up saving ~1.5 seconds on the builds I was benchmarking with:

|       | Baseline      | Patched       |
|-------|---------------|---------------|
| Rec   | 18.8 / 16.4 s | 15.1 / 15.2 s |
| Moore | 17.0 / 16.1 s | 14.2 / 14.7 s |


BEGINRELEASENOTES

- DD4hepConfig: look only for the Python interpreter when DD4hep was built without Geant4 (and not the development component)

ENDRELEASENOTES
